newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs weaken in late Tokyo, hit by hedge sales.
newsitem.headline: JGBs weaken in late Tokyo, hit by hedge sales.

text.p: JGBs weakened in both the cash and futures markets in late Tokyo trade on Tuesday on technical selling just before the futures market's close, traders said.
Several large offers, combining to total 300 contracts, hit the futures market just before the close at 0600 GMT, dragging September JGBs nearly to the day's low of 125.70, traders said.
Many said the large-lot selling reflected traders hedging against new purchases of four-year JGBs.
The Ministry of Finance offered 400 billion yen worth of 1.4 percent four-year JGBs through an auction, which produced a lowest price of 100.04 and an average price of 100.07.

In early afternoon trade, the key September contract temporarily eased after a remark by former senior Finance Ministry official Makoto Utsumi that JGBs are at a "bubble" level and do not reflect economic reality, traders said.
Utsumi, a former vice finance minister for international affairs who is now a professor at Keio University in Tokyo, said JGB prices are likely to undergo a downward correction.

"The JGBs dipped after (the) Utsumi (comments) but soon recovered ground, as many traders felt they did not have to pay too much attention to remarks made by a former government official," said a European bank trader.

Utsumi said that he did not understand why Japanese investors were so excessively cautious about putting money into Japanese equities, but added that sooner or later there would also be a correction in stock prices.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.190 percent, little changed from Monday's close of 2.185 percent.
Activity by overseas speculative accounts was subdued throughout the day, traders said.
The Bank of Japan carried out an accommodative operation in the money market on Tuesday, leaving the market with a sizable 300 billion yen surplus.
September JGBs ended at 125.72, down from Monday's close of 125.88. Turnover was 24,145 lots. The contract moved in a range of 125.70 to 125.93.
The September contract is expected to step down from its benchmark status in late August, traders said.
